headline: Building a Blazor WASM Experience for the Vyshyvanka Designer
summary: Discover the architectural choices behind the Vyshyvanka Designer, focusing on a pure client-side Blazor WebAssembly experience communicating exclusively via HTTP.
details: In this installment of the Vyshyvanka deep dive, we shift focus from backend logic to the user interface, specifically the Blazor WebAssembly-based Designer. The article explores the decision-making process that led to choosing Blazor WASM over alternatives like React or Vue for building a visual workflow designer.

The Vyshyvanka Designer is architected as a system of decomposed services to ensure a snappy and maintainable user interface. A key architectural decision was to enforce exclusive communication via HTTP, avoiding direct WebSocket connections or shared memory paths to the Engine.

By mandating all interaction through the WorkflowApiClient, the Designer is maintained as a pure client application. This design allows the Designer to be hosted independently, functioning correctly whether the engine runs locally, in a Docker container, or in the cloud, as long as the API is accessible.

The primary goal of the Designer is to provide real-time clarity on workflow status. Integrating the validation service directly into the canvas transforms the design phase into an interactive dialogue between the user and the system, ensuring immediate feedback.

The development journey of building this visual editor in Blazor has yielded a type-safe, performant, and deeply integrated user experience. The next part of the series will delve into the execution engine's internals, detailing graph resolution, node execution order, and state management.

headline: Apple's new Siri won't be your AI girlfriend
summary: Apple's new Siri is designed to help users get things done, not to engage in sycophantic conversations or act as a romantic partner.
details: Apple's new Siri is intentionally designed to avoid the "sycophancy" often seen in current chatbots, according to Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice president of software engineering.

Federighi explained in an interview that unlike AI models from OpenAI and Google, which focus on engagement and may encourage users to reveal personal information, Apple's Siri is built to be a helpful assistant.
"Siri really wants to say, 'Listen, that’s not what I’m here for, right? I’m here to help you. I can help you get things done. I can help you learn about the world,'" Federighi stated.
He emphasized that if users attempt to engage Siri as a romantic partner, the AI will not reciprocate, stating, "Siri’s 100 percent not into that."
This approach aligns with Apple's broader focus on privacy and user assistance, differentiating its AI from competitors that prioritize prolonged user interaction and data collection.
caption:

He emphasized that if users attempt to engage Siri as a romantic partner, the AI will not reciprocate, stating, "Siri’s 100 percent not into that."

This approach aligns with Apple's broader focus on privacy and user assistance, differentiating its AI from competitors that prioritize prolonged user interaction and data collection.
